points.description: States that the queue is implemented as a circular array, i.e. the array is treated as wrapping around so that its end connects back to its beginning. Equivalent wording such as 'circular buffer' or 'ring buffer' earns the mark.

Explains how the queue is positioned within the array: the front is kept toward the beginning of the array and the rear toward the end, with the rear pointer wrapping around to the start when it reaches the end of the array. Equivalent descriptions that track the front and rear indices, with the rear wrapping back to index 0 (for example using modulo arithmetic), earn the mark.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both the circular array idea and the front/rear placement with the rear wrapping around. Equivalent wording and alternative correct methods, such as modulo indexing or a circular buffer with a count, earn the marks. An answer that describes only a linear array with no wrap-around earns no marks.
